language.script_notes: Albanian (Shqip) is written in Latin script with the letters ë and ç, and the letter Ë/ë appears very frequently — a unique tell among its Balkan neighbours. The internet domain is .al.

road_furniture.km_marker_style: Chevron signs have white arrows on a black background, as in Greece and Italy. Street-name signs are Italian-style with dark backs.

architecture.roof_style: Flat concrete roofs, often topped with water tanks mounted on rooftops for storage and pumping.
architecture.roof_material: Flat concrete and red clay tile.
architecture.wall_construction: Concrete and red-brick houses, many left unfinished; Soviet- and Fascist-style concrete housing blocks repainted in rainbow colours in Tirana; small mushroom-shaped concrete bunkers everywhere.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Bright, sometimes clashing colours on repainted blocks, and bare brick and grey concrete elsewhere.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Concrete mushroom-shaped bunkers built between 1950 and 1985 — one for every four inhabitants, on the seashore, in front of houses, beside highways and on mountains, now turned into chicken coops, museums and cafés; colourful Tirana apartment blocks; the pyramid building in Tirana.

nature.vegetation: Olive groves and citrus on the coast, Mediterranean scrub on dry hills, and beech and pine forest in the mountains.
nature.terrain: Mountainous almost everywhere, with the rugged Albanian Alps in the north, hill and valley country in the south, and a narrow coastal plain on the Adriatic and Ionian seas.
nature.climate_signature: Mediterranean along the coast and cooler and snowier in the mountains.

vehicles.plate_color: White plates with blue bands on both sides, and red plates or red bands on taxis.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: German-made cars, especially Mercedes-Benz, make up around a third of registered vehicles.

google_coverage.blur_style: The Street View feed sometimes shows a thin black line across the image.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Blue-banded plates, Italian-style street signs, bollards and chevrons
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The letter Ë/ë and Albanian text settle it; Italian text and street names like 'Via' do not appear here, and the bunkers are found only here.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Neighbouring Balkan mountains and coasts, similar concrete architecture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Latin-script Albanian with Ë/ë is unique among these neighbours, and the mushroom bunkers are found only here.
